'''Zydrunas Ilgauskas''' ({{langx|lt|link=no|Žydrūnas Ilgauskas}}; {{IPA|lt|ʑiːˈdrûːnɐs ɪɫˈɡɐ̂ˑʊ̯skɐs|Lithuanian pronunciation|Zydrunas Ilgauskas.ogg}}; born June 5, 1975) is a Lithuanian-born American former professional [[basketball]] player who played the [[center (basketball)|center]] position. The {{height|ft=7|in=3}} Ilgauskas played for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] from 1997 to 2010<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1819826-cleveland-cavaliers-to-retire-zydrunas-ilgauskas-jersey|title=Cleveland Cavaliers to Retire Zydrunas Ilgauskas' Jersey|first=Grant|last=Hughes|website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> and played for the [[Miami Heat]] during the 2010–11 season. He was named to the 1997–98 All-Rookie First Team and is a two-time NBA All-Star. 

Ilgauskas played in the 2007 NBA Finals as a member of the Cavaliers. He is known for his accurate jump shot, for his rebounding, and for overcoming difficult injury challenges during his career.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/304682-zydrunas-ilgauskas-the-ups-and-downs-of-the-new-mr-cavalier|title=Zydrunas Ilgauskas: The Ups and Downs of the New Mr. Cavalier|first=Dan|last=Delagrange|website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> Nicknamed '''Big Z''',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/10576291/zydrunas-ilgauskas-no-11-jersey-retired-cleveland-cavaliers|title=Cavs honor 'Big Z' as LeBron makes cameo|date=March 9, 2014|website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref name="auto"/> Ilgauskas is the Cavaliers' career leader in [[Block (basketball)|blocked shots]];<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4707930|title=Ilgauskas finally sets Cavs record for games|date=December 3, 2009|website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cleveland Cavaliers Career Leaders |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/CLE/leaders_career.html |publisher=basketball-reference.com |access-date=November 24, 2021}}</ref> his jersey no. 11 has been retired by the team. In 2012, Ilgauskas joined the Cavaliers' front office, becoming a special advisor to the organization.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zydrunas Ilgauksas returns to Cavaliers in front office role |url=https://www.cleveland19.com/story/16546409/zydrunas-ilgauksas-returns-to-cavaliers-in-front-office-role/ |website=cleveland19.com |access-date=May 31, 2021 |date=January 18, 2012}}</ref><ref name = "Z">{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/cleveland-cavaliers-rumors-zydrunas-ilgauskas-133905256.html|title=Cleveland Cavaliers Rumors: Zydrunas Ilgauskas making a comeback?|date=August 25, 2014|work=Yahoo! Lithuanian professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is the head coach for [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe Beko]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. During his playing career, standing at a height of {{height|ft=6|in=4}} tall,[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=ADG&seasoncode=E2002 Sarunas Jasikevicius - Player profile.] he played at the [[point guard]] position. Often considered one of the best Lithuanian and European [[point guard]]s ever, Jasikevičius was a two-time [[All-EuroLeague First Team]] selection, the [[EuroLeague Final Four MVP]] in [[2005 EuroLeague Final Four|2005]] and a four-time [[European Basketball Triple Crown|triple crown]] winner. He was named the 2005 [[Israeli Basketball Premier League MVP]]. Moreover, he was the first player in [[EuroLeague]] history to win the competition with three clubs. A former representative of the senior [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuanian men's national team]], he won the gold medal at [[2003 EuroBasket]], earning an [[FIBA EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|All-EuroBasket Team]] selection and [[FIBA EuroBasket MVP|MVP honors]] in the process. He also won the bronze medal at the [[Basketball at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2000 Summer Olympic Games]], and the bronze medal at [[2007 EuroBasket]]. In 2015, Jasikevičius was named a [[EuroLeague Basketball Legend]] as a reward for his playing career[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5qqoiet33h95djia Sarunas Jasikevicius to be honored as Euroleague Basketball Legend] {{in lang|en}} and was honored with a ceremony.[https://web.archive.org/web/20150223011353/http://live.sportlive.co.za/?sport=news&page=news&view=article&news_id=545475 Real ruin Jasikevicius´ Euroleague legend induction, Barca bounce back.][https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sspzwPyLUoM Š.Jasikevičius oficialiai pripažintas Eurolygos legenda (VIDEO)] {{in lang|lt}} He has won both [[Liga ACB]] and [[Copa del Rey|Spanish Cup]] with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]] as both a coach and player, as well as both [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Basketball League]] and [[Turkish Basketball Cup|Turkish Cup]] with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] in same capacities. He also won the Euroleague title as Fenerbahçe coach in 2025. Additionally, he achieved victory in the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian League]] with [[BC Žalgiris|Zalgiris]], also as both coach and player.

'''İbrahim Kutluay''' (born 7 January 1974) is a former [[Turkish people|Turkish]] professional [[basketball]] player who has been a manager and pundit since his retirement.  He played the [[shooting guard]] position,<ref>{{cite web |title=İbrahim Kutluay Biyografisi |url=https://www.haberler.com/ibrahim-kutluay/biyografisi/ |website=haberler.com |access-date=15 February 2020}}</ref> and in his prime, was one of the most prolific 3-point shooters worldwide.<ref>{{cite news |date=6 May 2019 |title=Legend: Ibrahim Kutluay, Fenerbahce Beko Istanbul |url=https://www.adidasngt.com/final-four/vitoria-gasteiz-2019/news/i/9mydqm3quicx3ndu/legend-ibrahim-kutluay-fenerbahce-beko-istanbul |access-date=12 February 2020 |work=www.adidasngt.com |agency=}}</ref> He scored a record 50 points at the [[1996 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] against Italy,<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20140903112818/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/game/p/gid/6/grid/B/rid/1395/sid/2373/tid/376/_/1996_European_Championship_for_Men_22_and_Under_/statistic.html FIBA.com Game: ITALY vs TURKEY (Group B) Date: 1 July 1996.]</ref> and also 41 points in a [[EuroLeague]] game against [[Cibona Zagreb]] during the [[Euroleague 1998–99|1998–99 season]].<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.gameID_1756-E-14-5.compID_,Uz02qBnJiADOq5VntEf53.season_1999.roundID_2570.html FIBAEurope.com KK Cibona VIP 85-84 Fenerbahçe SK Date: 10.02.1999, 18:00h]</ref> He was the first Turkish basketball player to win the EuroLeague championship, winning the [[2002 EuroLeague Final Four]] with the Greek club [[Panathinaikos BC|Panathinaikos]]. Kutluay was the fourth Turk to play in the [[NBA]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Basketbolda Türkiyeyi Gururlandıran Kişiler |url=http://www.sportiveturkiye.com/genel/basketbolda-turkiyeyi-gururlandiran-kisiler/ |website=sportiveturkiye.com |date=27 November 2018 |access-date=13 February 2020}}</ref>  He is described as a 'stellar basketball player' whose 'legacy goes beyond his shooting skills, leadership, and incredible talent'.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gancedo |first1=Javier |title=Final Four interview: Ibrahim Kutluay |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/news/ |website=Euroleague.net |access-date=13 February 2020}}</ref> In addition to his professional career, he has also attracted interest as a high society figure due to his fame, wealth<ref>{{cite news |last1=Özgün |first1=Canan |date=2006-06-29 |title=Başka zevkim yok |url=http://www.milliyet.com.tr/otomobil/baska-zevkim-yok-539984 |access-date=12 February 2020 |agency=www.milliyet.com.tr}}</ref> and personal life<ref>{{cite news |last1=Çevik |first1=Emre |date=9 February 2020 |title=İbrahim Kutluay ilişkisi |url=https://www.sozcu.com.tr/hayatim/magazin-haberleri/ibrahim-kutluay-iliskisi-hakkinda-konustu/ |access-date=12 February 2020 |agency=www.sozcu.com.tr}}</ref> which has continuously been subjected to media scrutiny.<ref>{{cite news |date=2013-04-29 |title=İşte ünlülerin mal varlıkları |url=https://www.takvim.com.tr/galeri/saklambac/iste-unlulerin-mal-varliklari |access-date=12 February 2020 |agency=www.takvim.com.tr}}</ref>

'''Alejandro''' "'''Álex'''" '''Abrines Redondo''' (born 1 August 1993) is a Spanish former professional [[basketball]] player. He spent most of his career playing for [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]], acting as [[captain (sports)|team captain]] for several seasons. Standing at 6 ft 6 in (1.98 m), he mainly played the [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]] positions. Abrines has won three [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]] championships with FC Barcelona in [[2013–14 ACB season|2014]], [[2020–21 ACB season|2021]] and [[2022–23 ACB season|2023]]. He was selected for the [[EuroLeague Rising Star Award]] in 2016.

Born in [[Palma de Mallorca]], Spain, Abrines began his career with [[CB Axarquía]] in 2010, playing professionally till 2025. He joined [[Baloncesto Málaga]] in 2011 and was loaned back to Axarquía in the 2011–12 season. Abrines moved to FC Barcelona in 2012. He declared for the [[2013 NBA draft]] and was selected 32nd overall by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. After three more seasons with FC Barcelona, Abrines joined the Thunder in 2016 and played three seasons with the team. He returned to FC Barcelona in 2019.

Abrines has represented Spain internationally since his junior years. Abrines won a bronze medal with [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain]] at the [[2016 Summer Olympics]].

'''Zion Lateef Williamson''' (born July 6, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He plays the [[power forward]] position.<ref name="br">{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willizi01.html|title=Zion Williamson|publisher=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]|access-date=April 11, 2020}}</ref> Following a freshman-year stint with the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]], Williamson was selected by the Pelicans with the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]]. He was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] in 2020. In 2021, he became the fourth youngest NBA player to be selected to an All-Star game.<ref name="nba.com" /> Injuries have curtailed his subsequent NBA seasons.

Williamson attended [[Spartanburg Day School]], where he was a consensus five-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] and was ranked among the top five players in the 2018 class. He led his team to three straight state championships and earned [[South Carolina Mr. Basketball]] recognition in his senior season. Williamson also left high school as a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]], runner-up for [[Mr. Basketball USA]], and [[USA Today All-USA high school basketball team|''USA Today'' All-USA first team]] honoree. In high school, he drew national attention for his [[slam dunk]]s.

In his freshman and only season with Duke, Williamson was named [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]], [[ACC Athlete of the Year]] and [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|ACC Rookie of the Year]]. He set the single-game school scoring record for freshmen in January 2019, claimed ACC Rookie of the Week accolades five times, earned [[Associated Press College Basketball Player of the Year|AP Player of the Year]], [[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|''Sporting News'' College Player of the Year]] recognition, and won the [[USBWA National Freshman of the Year|Wayman Tisdale Award]].

'''Zavier Marquis Simpson''' (born February 11, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Ningbo Rockets]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]].

Simpson was a member of [[2017 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|2017]] and [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]] champions during his first two seasons. He had many of his best games against [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings|top-10]] opponents as a sophomore. As a junior, he was a [[2018–19 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2019]] Second team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] selection and a Big Ten All-Defensive team honoree and earned the nickname "Captain Hook" for his unusual skill at shooting [[hook shot]]s. As a senior, he was a [[2019–20 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2020]] Second team All-Big Ten selection. As a junior he set the current [[Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] single-tournament assists record (30) and led the Big Ten Conference in assists as a senior (7.9).
